subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired from his position as an investigator at Candlekeep but is now leading the effort to resolve Janussi’s murder, using academic protocol to avoid direct confrontation with Bookwyrm, hoping to preserve his future standing under the new leadership.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the current acting head of Candlekeep, suspected of concealing evidence in Janussi’s murder by moving the victim’s heart into the statue’s chalice, and is under threat of removal due to mounting suspicion — though her innocence has not been proven.
source_quote: She walks.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan’s Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi with a cleaver, but his confession does not explain who moved the heart or why — suggesting he is being used as a scapegoat to protect someone else.
source_quote: He'd killed Janussi.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the de facto leader of the group, focused on securing justice and reward, advocating for handing the case to Kalan to preserve his dignity after his firing, and pushing for tangible evidence — especially a magical book — to definitively implicate Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Alright. I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the linguistic and procedural analyst of the group, obsessively examining wording, spell mechanics, and protocol to expose loopholes — particularly in the Zone of Truth spell and Kalan’s academic reasoning.
source_quote: Sorry — how did he open that little diatribe? What was the first thing he said about the confession?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the pragmatic contingency planner, always ready with a fallback plan of violence — 'hacking and slashing' — as a safety net when diplomacy or academia fails.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Candlekeep Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the governing body of Candlekeep, currently divided by suspicion around Bookwyrm’s role in Janussi’s murder, with a naming ceremony imminent that may replace her with Fembris Lancer or another candidate, and whose internal politics are being manipulated by Kalan’s academic strategy.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a rival group whose legendary status overshadows the party, with exaggerated rumors and false posters in Gracklstugh bearing the party’s name — contributing to their infamy despite their desire to remain hidden.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard has a legend now that walks a tunnel ahead of us, and it lies about our height.

subject: Janussi’s murder investigation
fact: The investigation into Janussi’s murder has reached a turning point: Alkrist has confessed under magical compulsion, the heart was moved to a statue’s chalice, and Bookwyrm is the prime suspect for concealment — but no physical evidence directly ties her to the crime, forcing the group to rely on strategy over proof.
source_quote: You have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver.

subject: Candlekeep naming ceremony
fact: A formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, and Kalan believes the suspicion surrounding Bookwyrm will ensure she is not chosen — making her vulnerable to post-ceremony scrutiny and potential removal.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a revered library-fortress where scholarly authority and political power are intertwined; its internal politics are now the battleground for justice, with academic principles weaponized to avoid direct confrontation and preserve institutional stability.
source_quote: The reality is that all she did was hide a crime. She didn't commit one.

subject: cleaver
fact: The cleaver is the murder weapon used by Alkrist to kill Janussi, found at the scene and presented as physical evidence — but it only proves the act, not the conspiracy behind it.
source_quote: The cleaver proves someone covered this up cleverly.

subject: heart
fact: Janussi’s heart was removed from the body and placed inside the chalice of a statue — an act of concealment that suggests a deliberate effort to misdirect the investigation and protect someone else.
source_quote: She extracted the heart and put it in the chalice of the statue.

subject: Zone of Truth spell
fact: The Zone of Truth spell is a magical effect that compels honesty, but it is not infallible — it can be resisted with mental discipline, and its true value lies not in extracting truth, but in revealing whether someone *can* lie.
source_quote: The spell doesn't hand you the truth. It hands you the ability to watch someone refuse it.

subject: Kalan’s academic paper
fact: Kalan’s unpublished paper argues that a single source of truth — such as a confession — is insufficient for conclusive evidence; three independent types of proof are required — a standard that now shields Bookwyrm from conviction despite overwhelming suspicion.
source_quote: By the standard I wrote: she walks.

subject: the missing magical book
fact: Thorin and Kalan are searching for a powerful spellbook in Candlekeep’s library that could irrefutably prove Bookwyrm’s guilt — a book that, if found after the naming ceremony, could be granted by the new head as a tool of retribution rather than a weapon of accusation.
source_quote: I will come up with such a book before you leave.

subject: Dawnbringer’s therapy
fact: Dawnbringer, an entity linked to the party’s sword, insists on continuing therapeutic sessions to process the psychological toll of being bonded to a weapon — and has begun communicating telepathically with the narrator, suggesting a deeper, possibly magical connection.
source_quote: I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.

subject: the identity of Dawnbringer
fact: The nature of Dawnbringer — whether a sentient weapon, a spirit, or a psychological projection — remains ambiguous; the narrator struggles to determine her gender and origin, and her telepathic intrusions suggest she is more than a mere metaphor.
source_quote: I thought Dawnbringer was a she... I don't know, I can't remember.

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Candlekeep Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, marking the critical turning point in the political maneuvering around Bookwyrm’s fate.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: the sword whisperer
fact: The sword whisperer is an elusive figure sought by Dawnbringer — a being who understands the psychological trauma of sentient weapons — and whose absence has left Dawnbringer emotionally unmoored, driving her need for therapy.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is a likely candidate to replace Bookwyrm as head of the Avowed, suggested by Kalan as the next leader who would be more willing to pursue justice against Bookwyrm after the naming ceremony.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed...

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a figure of interest connected to the murder, with a thread running from the case back to him — but his role remains unclear, and the group has chosen not to confront him directly yet.
source_quote: We knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi, the deceased sage and former investigator, was the victim of the murder; his death triggered the investigation and his own rejected academic paper is now being used as a shield by Kalan to protect the guilty.
source_quote: And the person who declined it is dead. Janussi.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the observer and strategist who silently grifts the potion of flying using Glabbagool, marks the emotional deception of Bookwyrm, and documents the group's moral compromise — choosing embarrassment over murder as the crime to expose.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the manipulative Avowed leader who feigns grief and outrage while secretly relieved that Alkrist’s confession shields her — she orchestrates the group’s isolation, allows the safe to be sealed with incriminating evidence, and ensures her own elevation by appearing cooperative.
source_quote: Alkrist. I could never have imagined it.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan is the proceduralist who regains authority through the group’s actions, claims credit for their findings, and becomes the new First Keeper — his rigid adherence to method blinds him to Bookwyrm’s deception and the stolen evidence.
source_quote: It would seem, Kalan, that your methodology has proven its merit.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is Grygum’s sentient, acid-resistant ooze companion who absorbs liquids and magic, silently steals the potion of flying, and demonstrates nascent discipline by acting only on whispered instruction.
source_quote: Under the skin of my arm, Glabbagool liked the flying skill. He thought it was a good skill.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the passive observer and unwitting taster who, despite being under suspicion, remains naive and trusting — his consumption of the food serves as a risk-spending tool for the party’s survival calculus.
source_quote: Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed is the governing body of the academic society that has been infiltrated by deception; its members are quick to accept Alkrist’s confession, seal evidence without scrutiny, and elevate Bookwyrm’s authority — revealing systemic complacency and institutional blindness.
source_quote: The Avowed had all decided they'd won.

subject: safe opening
fact: The opening of Alkrist’s safe reveals a potion of flying, healing potion, gold, and a red herring coin — but no direct evidence of guilt, causing the Avowed to shift blame and abandon investigation, allowing Bookwyrm to control the narrative.
source_quote: Nothing else in there implicated Alkrist of anything.

subject: potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying is stolen by Grygum via Glabbagool during the chaos of the safe’s opening, concealed in the ooze, and removed from the scene without detection — becoming the party’s most valuable and hidden asset.
source_quote: While she's talking, my Glabbagool arm swipes the potion of flying off the table.

subject: red herring coin
fact: The red herring coin stamped with a herring is a deliberate red herring placed in Alkrist’s safe to mislead investigators — its presence signals that the owner had nothing to hide, reinforcing the illusion of innocence.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the book-filled chamber repurposed as a holding cell, where the party is confined under guard — symbolizing their entrapment within Bookwyrm’s narrative despite their successes.
source_quote: They put us in Deneir's office to wait out the evening.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient ooze entity bonded to Grygum, capable of absorbing liquids, resisting acid, and executing silent theft — its behavior reflects training, restraint, and emerging autonomy.
source_quote: He took it. A faint singe of acid, a small heat under the skin of my arm as he burned it away — only I felt it.

subject: Bookwyrm's true guilt
fact: The party possesses no proof that Bookwyrm committed the crime, only Alkrist’s accusation — leaving her guilt unresolved, her power intact, and the group’s moral stance reduced to a quiet grift rather than justice.
source_quote: We know who did it, someone said, and it's not her. Why wouldn't she be elected.

subject: Daral's curse
fact: Daral’s unresolved magical affliction lingers as a moral question — the party delays curing him, revealing their growing detachment and prioritization of self-interest over compassion.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?

subject: after the naming
fact: The official trial and judgment of Alkrist will occur after the naming ceremony, when the new head of the Avowed assumes power — delaying accountability and ensuring Bookwyrm’s influence endures.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the theatrical strategist who designs the group’s deception playbook — his obsession with dramatic arcs and closing reveals shapes the party’s actions, even as he fails to recognize their moral erosion.
source_quote: It'd be a good closing — she thought she got away with it, and then: one more thing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the observational tactician who applies narrative theory to interrogation — he detects the seam in Bookwyrm’s performance and advocates for withholding information to provoke deception, but remains passive in action.
source_quote: My take: be a little shy with the full details, but give enough to make it look like they could tell a story.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic warrior who relies on positioning, terrain, and weapon mastery, having survived a brutal ambush by helmed horrors and now seeking to unravel the mystery of the inert key that drew them.
source_quote: You don't chase, you position, and the ground under your feet says what your mouth doesn't need to.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a spellcaster who initially misjudged the nature of the helmed horrors but quickly adapted, realizing they were drawn to a key in his pocket — a key invisible to all detection magic.
source_quote: They don't have feelings. They have objectives.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a healer and support caster with abundant restoration and revival magic, who remains calm under pressure and provides unwavering backup to the party during combat.
source_quote: I also have Revivify, so we're covered either way.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combatant with strong physical prowess and a bond with Glabbagool, who uses grappling and acid to dismantle enemy armor, and is quick to analyze patterns in enemy behavior.
source_quote: If you're trying to hit him, you have advantage, because I grappled him.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is a passive observer who witnessed the key being passed and may hold critical but unacknowledged information about the ambush’s origin.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it? Fembris. Standing right there with the four of us.

subject: Unknown Architects of the Helmed Horrors
fact: An unseen faction designed and deployed helmed horrors as silent, untraceable assassins — creatures with no mouths, no minds, and no loyalty beyond a single objective: retrieve the inert key.
source_quote: Whoever built these chose them precisely so there'd be nobody to squeeze afterward.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors breached Deneir's Sanctum through windows, targeting Daz and later Grygum upon key transfer, ultimately destroyed by coordinated party efforts after revealing their mechanical, non-sentient nature.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a sealed chamber where the party was trapped during an ambush by helmed horrors, later left with shattered glass, dust, and two piles of ruined armor.
source_quote: Glass on the floor, dust settling, two dead heaps and one silent inert key three assassins had bled to reach.

subject: Inert Key
fact: An unmagical key, undetectable by all spells, that served as the sole target of the helmed horrors — its purpose and origin unknown, but clearly of immense value to its unseen owners.
source_quote: A key that read as nothing under every spell we'd thrown at it. Dead. Inert.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword that responded to Daral’s praise with visible emotional awakening, now a trusted weapon wielded by Thorin and possibly attuned to the party’s growing mystic resonance.
source_quote: Dawnbringer eats it up, I'm sure.

subject: Helmed Horror
fact: Helmed horrors are animated suits of plate armor with no occupants, capable of hovering and moving with eerie precision; they possess no sentience, speech, or emotion — only programmed objectives tied to the inert key.
source_quote: They're like AIs. A thing built to do one thing, that would do it until you stopped it, and no amount of talking would move it off.

subject: Origin of the Inert Key
fact: The key’s creation, purpose, and owners remain unknown — its only revealed trait is that it draws helmed horrors, suggesting it is either a beacon, a lock, or a fragment of something greater.
source_quote: Somebody built these, aimed them, and put them through the windows knowing exactly which pocket to reach for.

subject: Dawnbringer's Awakening
fact: Dawnbringer, once a weapon of last resort against fungus and undead, has been emotionally transformed by scholarly praise — now a sentient entity whose behavior may be changing in unpredictable ways.
source_quote: I watched the whole demeanor of the thing open up, and I thought, there it is, a small good thing in a room full of guards.

subject: Fembris’s Knowledge
fact: Fembris was the only one to see the key transferred — yet remained silent. Whether complicit, fearful, or simply unaware, their role in the ambush’s planning is unresolved.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it? Fembris.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during the continuation of a campaign session following the healing of Daral and the discovery of the helmed horrors’ ambush.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Grygum, Scene: Waiting in Deneir's Sanctum]

subject: Dawnbringer’s Lesser Restoration
fact: Dawnbringer performed a lesser restoration on Daral, curing his illness and triggering his epiphany about magical swords — an event that awakened the sword’s sentience and began a new dynamic between scholar and weapon.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is Zalthir’s acid-spewing companion that can dissolve metal armor, playing a critical role in dismantling the helmed horrors during combat.
source_quote: Glabbagool — riding his arm — did the acid trick. Plate hissed and ran.
